item.title: Quantum Haar Wavelet Transform methods applications and hardware realizations in quantum computing
item.description: Abstract Quantum Haar Wavelet Transform (QHWT) methods connect multiresolution analysis with quantum information processing through reversible averaging and differencing operations that can be implemented with comparatively compact circuits. Their localized basis functions, real-valued binary structure, and compatibility with hierarchical state representations make them attractive for resource-constrained quantum processing.

item.title: Complexity separations for optimal matchgate-Clifford synthesis
item.description: Clifford and matchgate circuits are canonical families of classically simulable quantum circuits. Their intersection, the matchgate-Clifford group, plays an important role in randomized fermionic protocols and in matchgate synthesis.

item.title: Can artificial systems become conscious?—Recursive embodied closure as an integrative framework
item.description: Recent advances in artificial intelligence, connectomics, and computational neuroscience increasingly raise the question of whether artificial systems—or even pure computer simulations—could become conscious. Contemporary theories emphasize embodiment, predictive processing, homeostatic regulation, and continuous interaction between cognition, body, and environment rather than isolated computation.

item.title: Toward quantum-informed addiction medicine: Coherence, entangled-photon imaging, and a theranostic hypothesis
item.description: BACKGROUND: Quantum biology has shown that selected biological processes depend on quantum effects, including coherence, tunnelling, and spin-dependent reactions. In parallel, quantum imaging now uses entangled photons to extract biological information at low photon flux.

item.title: Boundary-accessible work in a collision-charged topological quantum battery
item.description: Quantum batteries store energy in nonequilibrium quantum states. The ergotropy sets the work extractable by an arbitrary global unitary, but a device usually exchanges energy through a single local port.

item.title: CV-QAOA: Efficient Low-Depth Quantum Optimization of Continuous Variables
item.description: We study a Continuous-Variable Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (CV-QAOA) for high-dimensional continuous optimization. Our formulation extends an earlier CV-QAOA proposal with a variationally optimized initial state and recovers the convergence guarantees of Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD) in the high-depth limit.

item.title: Measurement-free Preparation of Surface-Code States with Digital-Analog Counterdiabatic Drivings
item.description: Preparing stabilizer-code states with shallow circuits is an important primitive for near-term quantum error correction in superconducting circuits, where logical-state initialization requires four-body stabilizer correlations from native one- and two-body controls. We introduce a digital-analog method for the preparation of surface-code ground-state manifolds.

item.title: AwarenessBench: Assessing Cognitive Capabilities of Language Models
item.description: As language models (LMs) exhibit increasingly consciousness-like behaviors, evaluating their cognitive abilities becomes essential. We introduce AwarenessBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for assessing the cognitive abilities of LMs in four dimensions: metacognition, self-awareness, social awareness, and situational awareness, covering 15 cognitive functions and 14,381 samples.

item.title: Virtual Reality Hypnosis: The Effectiveness of Virtual Reality Combined with Hypnotic Suggestions, a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
item.description: Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly used to support physical and mental health interventions. Recently, VR combined with hypnotic suggestions, termed virtual reality hypnosis (VRH), has emerged as a promising approach across clinical and non-clinical settings.

item.title: Quantum neuromorphic computing: harnessing noise and adaptation for scalable quantum processors
item.description: The von Neumann bottleneck and qubit fragility limit scalable computation. This review article synthesizes recent progress in a bio-inspired quantum approach that treats noise, dissipation, and dynamics as resources, drawing from neuroscience, neuromorphic design, and quantum biology.

item.title: Quantum statistical learning theory: concepts, regimes, and open problems
item.description: Statistical learning theory provides the mathematical foundations for understanding generalization from finite data. As quantum computing and quantum machine learning continue to develop, there is increasing interest in whether analogous principles can be formulated for learning settings involving quantum data, quantum models, or quantum computation.

item.title: Characterizing Photonic Partial Distinguishability Through Gram Matrix Tomography
item.description: Partial distinguishability affects multiphoton interference, which is central to large-scale photonic experiments such as Boson Sampling and to applications of multiphoton states across quantum technologies. Characterizing the internal degrees of freedom responsible for this behavior is challenging: in many scenarios they cannot be accessed directly and even their dimension or physical nature may be unknown \emph{a priori}.
